claims.text: The substitutional element X governs whether a stable, coherent protective oxide forms on CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C.
X governs protective-scale formation by affecting lattice mismatch and interfacial coherency between the oxide and alloy.
CrFeCoNiAl alloys are expected to form epitaxial, adherent protective oxides.
The protective oxides on CrFeCoNiAl may include Al2O3, potentially together with Cr2O3.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi develop oxides with higher lattice mismatch than CrFeCoNiAl.
The higher oxide–alloy lattice mismatch proposed for Mn- or Si-containing alloys leads to cracking or spallation.
The element X alters oxidation kinetics by influencing oxide-scale growth and structure.
In Al-containing alloys, reduced lattice mismatch promotes epitaxial growth of a continuous oxide scale.
Reduced lattice mismatch in Al-containing alloys promotes oxide-scale adhesion.
Oxides formed on Mn- or Si-containing alloys are less coherent and more susceptible to cracking or spallation.
Under identical exposure conditions, Al-containing alloys will form more continuous oxide layers than Mn- or Si-containing alloys.
Under identical exposure conditions, Al-containing alloys will form more coherent and adherent oxide layers than Mn- or Si-containing alloys.
Under identical exposure conditions, Mn- or Si-containing alloys will show more oxide-scale cracking or spallation than Al-containing alloys.
The proposed scope is limited to single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution CrFeCoNiX alloys exposed above 900 °C in controlled oxidative or corrosive atmospheres.

A failure of Al-containing alloys to show consistently lower lattice mismatch and a more coherent protective scale than Mn- or Si-containing alloys under identical conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
